subject: chemistry
title: Choosing conditions for industrial processes
key_idea: Industrial conditions are a compromise between rate, equilibrium yield and cost. In the Haber process a higher temperature speeds up the reaction but lowers the yield, a higher pressure raises both but costs more, and a catalyst speeds up the reaction without changing the yield. (Higher tier, Separate science)

sections.heading: Rate and yield (Higher tier, Separate science)

blocks.text: The Haber reaction is exothermic and reversible. Each condition affects the rate and the equilibrium yield differently.

items.meaning: How fast the reaction reaches equilibrium.
The amount of ammonia in the equilibrium mixture. A shift to the right gives more ammonia.

columns: Effect on equilibrium yield of ammonia
rows: Faster: more frequent collisions, and more particles have the activation energy
Lower: the equilibrium shifts left because the forward reaction is exothermic
Higher: the equilibrium shifts right because there are fewer molecules on the right-hand side
Faster: the activation energy is lowered
No effect on the position of equilibrium

items: A higher temperature speeds up the reaction but lowers the yield of an exothermic reaction.
A higher pressure speeds up the reaction and raises the yield when there are fewer molecules of gas on the right.
A catalyst speeds up the reaction but does not change the position of equilibrium.

sections.heading: Choosing the conditions (Higher tier, Separate science)

blocks.text: An industrial process must make enough product, fast enough, at an acceptable cost. The conditions are a compromise.

items: Raw materials and energy supplies must be available and affordable.
A higher temperature uses more energy, so it increases costs.
A higher pressure uses more energy and needs stronger reaction vessels, so it increases costs.
A catalyst increases the rate and reduces energy costs.
Recycling unreacted gases makes use of all the raw materials.
On a graph of product against time, a steeper line means a faster rate. The line levels off when equilibrium is reached.
Temperature: a low temperature gives a better yield but a slow rate. A high temperature gives a fast rate but a low yield and a high cost. 450 °C is a compromise.
Pressure: a higher pressure gives a better yield and rate, but costs more. 200 atmospheres is a compromise between yield, rate and cost.
The aim is an acceptable yield in an acceptable time.
Conditions are chosen for an acceptable yield in an acceptable time at an acceptable cost.
Higher temperature and higher pressure both increase energy costs.
The temperature and pressure used are compromises.

checks.q: State the effect of increasing the temperature on the rate and on the equilibrium yield of ammonia.
checks.a: The rate increases. The equilibrium yield decreases, because the forward reaction is exothermic and the equilibrium shifts to the left.

checks.q: State the effect of an iron catalyst on the position of equilibrium.
checks.a: None. It only increases the rate of reaction.

checks.q: Explain why a pressure much higher than 200 atmospheres is not used.
checks.a: It uses more energy and needs stronger, more expensive reaction vessels, so costs increase.

mistakes.wrong: A higher temperature gives a higher yield of ammonia.
mistakes.right: The reaction is exothermic, so a higher temperature shifts the position of equilibrium to the left. The rate is higher, but the yield is lower.

mistakes.wrong: The catalyst increases the yield of ammonia.
mistakes.right: A catalyst has no effect on the position of equilibrium. It lowers the activation energy and increases the rate, and it reduces energy costs.

mistakes.wrong: The highest possible pressure should be used because it gives the most ammonia.
mistakes.right: A higher pressure uses more energy and needs stronger reaction vessels, which increases costs. The pressure chosen is a compromise between yield, rate and cost.

worked_example.question:
The equation for the production of ammonia in the Haber process is:

N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)

The forward reaction is exothermic.

The conditions used are:
- a temperature of 450 °C
- a pressure of 200 atmospheres
- the presence of an iron catalyst.

Explain why these conditions are chosen for economical production of ammonia in the Haber process.

You should include references to the rate of reaction and the position of equilibrium.
answer_points: Rate: a higher temperature gives a higher rate because of more frequent collisions and more particles with the activation energy.
Rate: a higher pressure gives a higher rate because of more frequent collisions. The catalyst gives a higher rate because it lowers the activation energy.
Equilibrium: a higher temperature shifts the position of equilibrium to the left because the reaction is exothermic.
Equilibrium: a higher pressure shifts it to the right because there are more molecules on the left-hand side. The catalyst has no effect on the position.
Cost: higher temperature or pressure uses more energy, and a higher pressure needs stronger vessels. A catalyst reduces energy costs.
Compromise: the temperature is a compromise between rate, equilibrium position and cost. The pressure is a compromise between yield, rate and cost.
worked_example.tip: Marked in levels. The top level needs the points to be detailed and logically linked in a clear account.

mistakes.wrong: The catalyst increases the equilibrium yield of products.
mistakes.right: A catalyst increases the rate of attainment of equilibrium, but has no effect on the equilibrium yield.

mistakes.wrong: The catalyst lowers the activation energy.
mistakes.right: On its own this is ignored when the question asks for the effect on the rate of attainment of equilibrium and on the yield. Say the rate is increased and the yield has no change.

mistakes.wrong: A higher pressure only makes the reaction faster.
mistakes.right: It also increases the equilibrium yield. The equilibrium shifts to the right because there is a decrease in the number of molecules.

worked_example.question:
Ammonia is manufactured by the Haber process.
The equation for the reaction is
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)
The reaction is reversible and can reach equilibrium.

The reaction is carried out at a pressure of 200 atmospheres.
Explain what effect a pressure higher than 200 atmospheres would have on the rate of attainment of equilibrium and on the equilibrium yield of ammonia.
answer_points: Equilibrium is attained in a shorter time, so the rate of attainment of equilibrium increases.
The equilibrium yield of ammonia increases.
The equilibrium shifts to the right, towards the products.
Because there is a decrease in the number of molecules (four molecules of gas become two).
worked_example.tip: One mark each. Moving to fewer molecules is allowed in place of the last point.

mistakes.wrong: Conditions B are better because the higher pressure increases the rate of reaction.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Use equilibrium too: pressure does not change the position when there are the same number of molecules on both sides.

mistakes.wrong: At a lower pressure the reaction will not be at equilibrium.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Say the rate of reaction is slower, or the yield of ammonia is less, because the equilibrium shifts left to the side with more molecules.
A catalyst does not affect the position of equilibrium. It increases the rate of reaching equilibrium.

worked_example.question:
A company makes hydrogen iodide, HI, gas by reacting hydrogen gas with iodine gas.

H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)

The forward reaction is exothermic.

The yield of hydrogen iodide and the rate at which the reaction reaches equilibrium are affected by different conditions.

The table shows two possible reaction conditions, A and B.

| | Temperature (°C) | Pressure (atmospheres) | Catalyst? |
| A | 450 | 1 | Yes |
| B | 700 | 3 | No |

The company decides to use reaction conditions A, instead of B.

Explain why they make this choice.

Use ideas about rate of reaction and position of equilibrium to help you.
answer_points: The lower temperature in A moves the position of equilibrium to the right, giving a higher yield, because the forward reaction is exothermic.
The rate is faster in B because of the higher temperature. A uses a compromise temperature.
Higher pressure in B does not affect the position of equilibrium, because there are the same number of molecules on both sides.
The catalyst in A does not affect the position of equilibrium, but increases the rate of reaching equilibrium.
worked_example.tip: Any four. Unqualified answers are taken to refer to A.
